questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: A large dam has come up on a river on which a whole district depends for floodplain farming. A student has to explain, step by step, how regulating and damming the river has affected the river’s own flow, the stream beds and the aquatic habitats, and the fertility of the floodplains. Set the chain out in steps.

markingPoints.description: Regulating and damming of rivers affects their natural flow, causing poor sediment flow
It leads to excessive sedimentation at the bottom of the reservoir
This results in rockier stream beds
The rivers’ aquatic life is left with poorer habitats
The floodplains are deprived of silt, a natural fertiliser, further adding to the problem of land degradation

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Step 1: Regulating and damming of rivers affects their natural flow, causing poor sediment flow. Step 2: This leads to excessive sedimentation at the bottom of the reservoir. Step 3: The result is rockier stream beds. Step 4: The rivers’ aquatic life is left with poorer habitats. Step 5: Sedimentation also meant that the floodplains were deprived of silt, a natural fertiliser, further adding to the problem of land degradation.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
A farmer named Raghu lives in the Damodar valley, where a song sung at Bhadu tells how the crops were sown in Asar and how the floods swollen the Damodar stop the sailing boats from sailing, so the people fall at the river’s feet and ask it to reduce the floods a little. Downstream, a large dam now regulates the river. Raghu notices that the stream beds have turned rocky, that fish no longer move upstream as they once did to spawn, and that the fields on the floodplain no longer receive the silt that used to make them rich.

(a) Raghu’s grandfather remembers a Bhadu song about the Damodar; give the name of the river and the name by which that river is known. (b) Raghu says the dam has taken the richness out of his fields. Using what dams do to sediment, and what the floodplains are deprived of, explain why his fields are poorer and what he stands to lose.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (a) The Damodar, known as the river of sorrow. (b) Damming the river causes poor sediment flow and collects excessive sedimentation at the bottom of the reservoir, so the floodplains are deprived of silt, a natural fertiliser, further adding to land degradation. Raghu stands to lose the fertility of his fields.
